feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — This encoding represents the abstract credential, not the printed diploma.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — A university degree is a formalized, human-invented institutional system.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not derived from biology or biomimicry.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Not dependent on energy or activation.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Provides no physical support or mechanical structure.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — The credential is symbolic and abstract; instantiations are secondary.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Stored digitally or on paper, but its core identity is symbolic.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Cannot initiate behavior or change by itself.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — It is constructed to formalize achievement, confer qualifications, and structure access.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — The degree does not generate output autonomously.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — It is data to be interpreted, not a logic processor.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — It denotes a status, but does not itself enact transformation.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Interpreted and used by humans, but not directly interactive.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Relevant in systems, but not embedded as a functional unit.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — It has no independent action; requires institutional context.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Many social functions occur outside credentialing systems.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Encodes abstract meaning and social status.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Primary purpose is to communicate academic qualification and institutional endorsement.
feedback.Rule-governed: Excluded — Issuance follows rules, but the degree itself does not encode operational logic.
feedback.Compositional: Excluded — Not meaningfully constructed from modular components.
feedback.Normative: Included — Defines expectations about competence, achievement, and role eligibility.
feedback.Meta: Excluded — Does not reference its own structure or type.
feedback.Temporal: Excluded — Although issued at a moment in time, the degree is not time-dependent in structure.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Often exists in institutional databases and credential platforms.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists entirely through collective agreement and institutional legitimacy.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Can only be granted by accredited universities or equivalent institutions.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Included — Tied to personal identity, used in employment, status, and records.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Governed by accreditation bodies and educational regulations.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Affects income, opportunity, labor markets, and access.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Central to political discourse on access, merit, class, and educational policy.
feedback.Ritualised: Excluded — Participates in rituals (e.g., graduation), but is not itself a ritualized entity.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Raises issues of fairness, privilege, access, and meritocracy.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the university degree as an abstract institutional credential — not a physical document. It is a symbolic, regulated, and identity-linked construct, designed to signal achievement and confer access. Its social and ethical significance is tightly bound to its legitimacy and role in economic and political systems.
